subject_name: Aircraft Wiring Practices (Electrical wiring and Interface system)
topic: Control horizontal and vertical movement, control of RPM, torque reaction, tail rotor compensations, contra rotating rotors.
syllabus_extract: Control horizontal and vertical movement, control of RPM, torque reaction, tail rotor compensations, contra rotating rotors.
specific_objectives: 12.1.4.1 Trainee will be able to explain horizontal and vertical movement, torque reaction, tail rotor compensations, contra rotating rotors.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of cyclic and collective control inputs, torque reaction principles, tail rotor compensation mechanisms, and contra-rotating rotor configurations. Safety: Ensure no loose items near workspace. Instructor supervision: Monitor trainee understanding of rotational dynamics.
intro_questions: What are the primary functions of the cyclic and collective controls?
How does torque reaction affect the helicopter fuselage?
Why are contra-rotating rotors used in certain helicopter designs?

topics: Control of RPM via collective pitch
development.content:
Horizontal and vertical movement control
Control of RPM via collective pitch
Torque reaction and fuselage rotation

Tail rotor compensations for torque
Pedal control for yaw movement
Efficiency of tail rotor systems

Contra rotating rotors design
Cancellation of torque effects
Advantages of coaxial systems

summary_questions: Explain how the tail rotor compensates for torque reaction.
Describe the mechanism of contra-rotating rotors in eliminating torque.
How does the pilot control vertical movement using the collective?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the differences between single main rotor and contra-rotating rotor systems, referencing concepts covered in LP 02.

pft_rows.syllabus: Main rotor movements, symmetry of lift feathering, flapping, dragging, hook’s joint effect, flapping to equality, phase lag and advance angle concepts.
